anomalies.description: A person enters the store, walks toward the right side near shelves, and appears to conceal an item (possibly in clothing or a bag) before moving toward the exit. Their posture and hand placement suggest deliberate concealment behavior consistent with shoplifting. The individual exits the frame near the door within seconds, without interacting with staff or making a visible purchase.

anomalies.description: A second person enters the store through the glass door while the first person is standing near display boxes; the entering individual appears to be holding an item close to their body in a manner suggestive of concealment (e.g., tucking under arm or into clothing), and proceeds toward the interior without placing the item down or interacting with staff. The timing and behavior—entering while another person is present near merchandise, combined with possible concealment—aligns with shoplifting indicators. No clear evidence of violence, vandalism, or other crimes observed.

A man enters the store carrying a large, dark rectangular object (likely a box or electronic device) that was not visible outside; he walks directly toward the interior while another person observes near a display. The object appears to be concealed under his arm or against his torso as he moves inward, consistent with shoplifting behavior—specifically, concealing merchandise upon entry or immediately after entering, rather than placing it in a shopping cart or basket. No legitimate transaction or interaction with staff is observed.

A person in an orange shirt and dark apron (likely a staff member or customer) moves from near the counter toward the left side of the frame and exits the view while holding an object close to their body; shortly after, a second person in a patterned shirt remains near the counter, looking down and appearing to manipulate or conceal something in their hands or clothing. The sequence suggests possible concealment of merchandise, especially given the context of retail store entry/exit proximity and the timing of movements coinciding with the first person leaving the field of view. No clear theft is visible, but behavior is suspicious and consistent with shoplifting preparation/concealment.
